root_cause.text: KVM SVM's INVLPGA instruction emulation did not check whether EFER.SVME is set, allowing the instruction to execute even when SVME is disabled, instead of injecting a #UD (Undefined Instruction) exception as required by the AMD architecture.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a call to `nested_svm_check_permissions(vcpu)` inside `invlpga_interception()`. The commit message explicitly states: "INVLPGA should cause a #UD when EFER.SVME is not set. Add a check to properly inject #UD when EFER.SVME=0." The diff shows: `+ if (nested_svm_check_permissions(vcpu)) return 1;` which triggers a VM exit (return 1) when the permission check fails, leading to #UD injection.
